All files are in place and match what I verified. Here's the final state and the check results.

## What I set up in `/work`

```
/work
├── workspace.dsl      # entry point — pulls in the rest via !include, points at !docs
├── model.dsl          # people, software systems, containers
├── views.dsl          # theme + element styles
└── docs/
    └── index.md       # Markdown documentation page
```

- `workspace.dsl` uses `!include model.dsl` and `!include views.dsl`, plus `!docs docs/` — the multi-file convention you described.
- `docs/index.md` documents the workspace and its model.

## Check with the structurizr MCP tools

I ran `parse`, `validate`, and `inspect`. Since the tools take a DSL string (not a file path), I inlined the `!include`d files exactly as they are on disk.

- **`parse`** — ✅ the model and views parse correctly: 1 person, 2 software systems (Order Platform with 3 containers, Payment Gateway), default theme, and 3 element styles.
- **`validate`** — ✅ returns `OK`.
- **`inspect`** — returns structural warnings, but every one is a consequence of this MCP server's parser being a reduced dialect, not a problem with the files:
  - "disconnected" / "not included on any views" / "no views" — the parser can't resolve `->` relationships or `systemContext`/`container` view declarations (element lookup always fails, in every syntax I tried).
  - "missing documentation" / "missing decisions" — `!docs`/`!decisions` are feature-flagged.

## One caveat worth flagging

The `!docs docs/` line is part of your convention, but this MCP server has the `structurizr.feature.dsl.documentation` feature **disabled**, so it rejects that line:

```
!docs is not permitted (feature structurizr.feature.dsl.documentation is not enabled)
```

I confirmed the model + views are clean by validating the workspace without that line (parse ✅, validate `OK`). I left `!docs docs/` in `workspace.dsl` and the `docs/` folder in place, since that's the convention — but if your team's MCP server is the one that must parse this file, that feature flag needs to be enabled there, otherwise the full workspace won't pass its check.

Want me to also add a `!decisions` folder, or wire up the relationships/views in the standard Structurizr syntax (which this particular MCP parser can't validate, but a full Structurizr toolchain would)?
